readme.text:
AngularJS
=========

AngularJS lets you write client-side web applications as if you had a smarter browser. It lets you
use good old HTML (or HAML, Jade/Pug and friends!) as your template language and lets you extend HTML’s
syntax to express your application’s components clearly and succinctly. It automatically
synchronizes data from your UI (view) with your JavaScript objects (model) through 2-way data
binding. To help you structure your application better and make it easy to test, AngularJS teaches
the browser how to do dependency injection and inversion of control.

It also helps with server-side communication, taming async callbacks with promises and deferred objects,
and it makes client-side navigation and deep linking with hashbang urls or HTML5 pushState a
piece of cake. Best of all? It makes development fun!

--------------------

**AngularJS support has officially ended as of January 2022.
[See what ending support means](https://docs.angularjs.org/misc/version-support-status)
and [read the end of life announcement](https://goo.gle/angularjs-end-of-life).**

**Visit [angular.io](https://angular.io) for the actively supported Angular.**

--------------------

* Web site: https://angularjs.org
* Tutorial: https://docs.angularjs.org/tutorial
* API Docs: https://docs.angularjs.org/api
* Developer Guide: https://docs.angularjs.org/guide
* Contribution guidelines: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
* Core Development: [DEVELOPERS.md](DEVELOPERS.md)
* Dashboard: https://dashboard.angularjs.org

Documentation
--------------------
Go to https://docs.angularjs.org

Contribute
--------------------

We've set up a separate document for our
[contribution guidelines](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Develop
--------------------

We've set up a separate document for
[developers](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/master/DEVELOPERS.md).

What to use AngularJS for and when to use it
---------
AngularJS is the next generation framework where each component is designed to work with every other
component in an interconnected way like a well-oiled machine. AngularJS is JavaScript MVC made easy
and done right. (Well it is not really MVC, read on, to understand what this means.)

#### MVC, no, MV* done the right way!
[MVC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model%E2%80%93view%E2%80%93controller), short for
Model-View-Controller, is a design pattern, i.e. how the code should be organized and how the
different parts of an application separated for proper readability and debugging. Model is the data
and the database. View is the user interface and what the user sees. Controller is the main link
between Model and View. These are the three pillars of major programming frameworks present on the
market today. On the other hand AngularJS works on MV*, short for Model-View-_Whatever_. The
_Whatever_ is AngularJS's way of telling that you may create any kind of linking between the Model
and the View here.

Unlike other frameworks in any programming language, where MVC, the three separate components, each
one has to be written and then connected by the programmer, AngularJS helps the programmer by asking
him/her to just create these and everything else will be taken care of by AngularJS.…

causeOfDeath.headline: A web framework giant formally retired after reaching its official end-of-life.
causeOfDeath.explanation: AngularJS did not die from project abandonment or lack of adoption, but via scheduled deprecation by its maintainers. Official support ended in January 2022, steering the web development ecosystem toward the rebuilt Angular platform.

timeOfDeath.note: Substantive maintenance ended with the 1.8.3 changelog release updates, with subsequent commits limited to link maintenance.

diagnosis.evidence: README explicitly states 'AngularJS support has officially ended as of January 2022' and directs users to angular.io for active support.
Modern web architecture moved away from digest cycles and legacy MV* patterns toward component-based frameworks, leading maintainers to focus on the full rewrite of Angular.

worthSaving: Pioneering concepts of declarative HTML templates and client-side dependency injection
Comprehensive documentation framework and testing methodologies established across karma and protractor configs

marketToday.reasoning: The modern frontend ecosystem has standardized around modern component architectures like React, modern Angular, Vue, and Svelte. The 2010-era digest cycle and implicit two-way data binding have been superseded by explicit unidirectional data flows.

autopsy.revivalScoreReason: The framework reached its deliberate End of Life and was officially archived by Google in favor of modern Angular.
autopsy.epitaph: It taught the browser HTML extensions, then passed the torch.

resurrection.honestNote: AngularJS reached official End-of-Life in January 2022 and its architecture cannot compete with modern frontend frameworks today. We are pivoting to salvage its core strength—declarative HTML extensions and simple client-side dependency injection—into a lightweight, zero-build micro-library for modern HTML-first web apps.

Legacy HTTP deferred/promise abstractions — because native async/await and fetch exist
Complex MV* scope hierarchies — because modern flat state stores scale better

crowdfundingPitch.title: HTML-Inject: Reviving Declarative HTML for the Modern Web
crowdfundingPitch.story: I spent years watching the web ecosystem evolve, but I never forgot the magic of the early days of AngularJS. It officially died in January 2022, after reaching its scheduled end-of-life. It wasn't abandoned; it was replaced by a more complex successor that required massive build pipelines and a total shift in mental models. While the world moved to modern Angular and React, the original dream of simply extending HTML with data-binding became a relic of the past. The autopsy is clear: the heavy digest cycles and legacy MV* patterns couldn't keep up with modern performance standards. I am salvaging the best parts—the pioneering concepts of declarative HTML templates and dependency injection—and stripping away the bloat. I am rebuilding this as a modern ESM library under 5KB that requires no build step. This is for the builders who want to enhance HTML without being forced into a heavy framework silo. It is an honest revival of a dead giant's soul, optimized for 2026.
fundingUse: Fund comprehensive cross-browser testing infrastructure for the core engine
Design and host a library of interactive documentation sandboxes
Maintain a high-performance global CDN for zero-build distribution
crowdfundingPitch.backerReward: Founding Backer recognition in the project README and a vote on the priority of new HTML directives

resurrection.aiBuildPrompt: Rebuild the core architectural concepts of AngularJS—specifically declarative HTML reactivity and dependency injection—into a tiny, modern micro-library called HTML-Inject. Use ES6 JavaScript DOM Proxies and MutationObserver for reactivity instead of the legacy $digest cycle. The library must be a single-file ESM module under 5KB. It should allow users to add attributes like x-model for two-way form binding and x-bind for dynamic text updates directly in plain HTML without any build step or compilation. The target user is a solo indie hacker building lightweight, server-rendered web apps (like with HTMX or Laravel) who needs light client-side interactivity without a heavy Node.js toolchain. Do not include legacy browser fallbacks, jQuery dependencies, or complex promise abstractions; use native fetch and async/await. Implement a simple registry-based dependency injection container for managing stateful services. Definition of done: provide the core ESM script and an index.html file that demonstrates a working live reactive form, a list renderer using x-repeat, and a service injected via the DI container, all working together in the browser with just a single script tag inclusion.
